title: Application Configuration
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of application configuration in a C#/.NET program.
Predict the result of the included C# example and verify the documented output.
Apply application configuration to a small task and identify one relevant boundary, limitation, or version requirement.

content.intro: Application Configuration is lesson 148 in The .NET Project and Package Ecosystem. File and data APIs cross boundaries where permissions, encodings, invalid data, resource lifetime, and partial failures matter.
content.why_it_matters: Reproducible builds depend on explicit project settings and consistent dependency management. This lesson focuses on application configuration and shows how to verify the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

content_blocks.title: A practical way to learn it
content_blocks.text: Start with the smallest valid case for application configuration. Predict the output, run or inspect the example in the stated toolchain, then change one input or rule and compare the result. For production code, record assumptions and verify boundary cases.

items.title: Environment-specific configuration
items.text: Keep environment-specific configuration outside source code. Read settings at a clear boundary, validate required values on startup, and never commit credentials or print them in diagnostics.

items.title: App configuration files
items.text: Keep environment-specific configuration outside source code. Read settings at a clear boundary, validate required values on startup, and never commit credentials or print them in diagnostics.

items.title: Environment variables
items.text: A variable has a type, a current value, and a scope. Initialize it before use, limit its lifetime where possible, and make state changes visible so later code can reason about it.

items.title: Command-line arguments
items.text: Treat a design pattern as a response to a recurring problem, not as a required layer. Explain the problem first, choose the smallest useful design, and keep refactoring protected by tests.

items.title: Separating configuration from code
items.text: Keep environment-specific configuration outside source code. Read settings at a clear boundary, validate required values on startup, and never commit credentials or print them in diagnostics.

items.title: Protecting secrets
items.text: Define trust boundaries, store secrets outside source, fail safely, and verify the release artifact in the target environment.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small C# example that demonstrates application configuration. Change one input or implementation detail, predict the result, then check it locally and explain one edge case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates application configuration rather than only repeating its definition.
The result is checked locally or against a clearly documented reference output.
At least one relevant boundary, invalid-input case, or compatibility condition is considered.
hints: List the assumptions and expected behavior for application configuration before editing the code.
Change one variable or rule at a time; keep the previous output for comparison.
If behavior differs, confirm the compiler/target framework and consult the linked official documentation.
content.solution_notes: Suggested approach: identify the expected input and output, start from the smallest example, use the feature only where it clarifies the rule, and verify both a typical case and a boundary/failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming the feature works identically on every target
common_mistakes.why: Language syntax, libraries, and runtime support are version-dependent.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the target framework and official versioned reference before using the feature.

common_mistakes.why: Boundary values, malformed input, and failure states often expose the real bug.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one typical input and one boundary or invalid case to the manual or automated checks.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating sample output as proof that the code ran
common_mistakes.why: The course reader uses static reference output for C# because it has no C# execution runner.
common_mistakes.fix: Run the snippet in a local .NET project or a separately isolated execution service.
